# DSH A2UI Studio
**Your agent manages. A2UI Studio remembers.**
A DeepSeek Harness plugin for delegating machine and application management to your agent. Describe
the target and the job; the agent can register the machine, investigate its applications, save what
matters, and build an interface you can use again.
中文 · Download v0.3.2 · Setup · End-to-end walkthrough
## 1. Tell the agent what to manage
> “Register this machine as Queue server. Find the queue application and remember where it lives.”
The agent checks existing records and uses `machine_manage` to create or update the machine archive.
Supply connection details through your approved access setup when needed; manual registration is an
optional fallback, not a prerequisite.
*8 seconds · Review the completed agent registration and open its saved record.*
## 2. Turn application knowledge into a working panel
> “Show running, waiting, completed and failed jobs, with concurrency. Start read-only.”
The agent reads the application, records its location and purpose, and proposes a tailored card. You
review the execution definitions before publication; the plugin keeps the notes, card versions and
on definitions before publication; the plugin keeps the notes, card versions and operation receipts.
*8 seconds · Inspect the saved application notes and refresh the published panel.*
## 3. Use it directly—or delegate the next job
Open the machine to use its saved panel. Click **@** when you want the agent to investigate or chang
e something; it can retrieve the existing context instead of starting from scratch.
*7.5 seconds · Attach the machine to chat; no new request is submitted.*
*Three short recordings of real DSH, using fictional local demo data. Completed results are revisite
d, not presented as live generation. Details and still images.* The plugin keeps knowledge the agent
explicitly saves; it does not automatically remember every conversation.
Another application: dual-GPU monitoring and power controls. The same workflow can leave you a very
different interface.
## What is included
| Capability | What it gives you |
| Machine directory | Persistent records, multiple SSH paths, default connection, health checks, and

@ references |
| Application cards | Model-authored layouts, data bindings, conditional controls, a

nd numeric color scales |
| Persistent operations | Card revisions, publication review, execution pe

rmissions, and action receipts |
| Extensible UI | A component catalog plus custom card extensions w

hen standard components are insufficient |
| Agent skills | Machine management, card authoring, and
extension development guidance shipped with the plugin |
The UI follows an **A2UI-inspired** approach: the agent describes a structured interface and the hos
t renders it. This is not a claim of full A2UI protocol compatibility. Custom extensions are a separ
ate, code-bearing capability and should be reviewed accordingly.
## Install
Previously called DSH Control Studio. The install/package ID remains `dsh-control-studio` for compat
ibility; existing installations need no migration for this branding change.
**Prerelease. Linux and Windows desktop; DSH `0.2.1-alpha.1` / `0.2.1-rc.2`.** See Windows setup and
limits. Independent community project, not an official DeepSeek plugin.

## Start with a read-only card
Already using `dsh-machine-apps`? Follow the rename migration guide before installing. Do not enable
both packages together.
Ask the agent to use `machine-management` to register the target and record its connection, then `ap
p-cards-authoring` to inspect the application and propose a read-only panel. For a machine already i
n the directory, reference it with @. Add controls after confirming what each action executes.
